::: {.why}
The seat you are aiming for, described honestly: no individual trade is convincing, and the entire edge is that you have several hundred of them and they are close to independent.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the relationship between a signal's hit rate, the number of independent bets and the resulting information ratio, and say which of the three is easiest to improve.
- Say what the original pairs trading result was, when it stopped working, and what that pattern predicts about anything you publish.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Read the Gatev, Goetzmann and Rouwenhorst pairs trading paper, sections on the trading rule and the results. Skip the robustness appendices. Note the sample period and the reported excess return.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} The breadth arithmetic, which is the single most useful piece of algebra in this phase: with a per-bet correlation between forecast and outcome of 0.03 and N independent bets a year, the annual information ratio is roughly 0.03 times the square root of N. Solve for the N that gives an information ratio of 1. Then say what happens to that N when your bets are correlated at 0.3 rather than 0.
:::
:::
